newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas welcomes Canal Plus pact.
newsitem.headline: Havas welcomes Canal Plus pact.

text.p: French media group Havas said on Friday that it welcomed a merger between French subscriber television company Canal Plus and Dutch satellite television company Nethold.

Havas, currently the largest shareholder in Canal Plus with a 24 percent stake, added in a statement that it was confident it could, in consultation with its partners, maintain the same scale of investment in the new company.
"Havas, Canal Plus' largest stakeholder, fully approves the conclusion of an agreement between Canal Plus and Nethold," Havas said in the statement.
"It is obvious that, within the appropriate time-frame, Havas will once again find itself in the position it formerly held among Canal Plus shareholders," Havas said.
Nethold is jointly held by Richemont SA, which is quoted on the Zurich and Johannesburg stock exchanges, and MIH Holdings Ltd, a listed holding company.
The new group will have significant positions in France, Italy, Spain, Scandinavia, the Benelux countries and Germany, as well as a presence in many central European markets.
Utilities group Cie Generale des Eaux, another key shareholder in Canal Plus, said earlier it too was delighted with the merger plan.

Generale des Eaux said it was comfortable with its investment in Canal Plus and, in agreement with other Canal Plus shareholders, it would seek to maintain the same scale of investment in the new firm after the merger.

Under the terms of the deal, Canal Plus will buy 100 percent of Nethold from Richemont and MIH, paying with 6.1 million new Canal Plus shares and $45 million in cash. Following the issue of new Canal Plus shares, Richemont and MIH will repectively own 15 and five percent of Canal Plus.
The merger is subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
